source.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ כִּֽי־הֵחֵ֣ל הָֽאָדָ֔ם לָרֹ֖ב עַל־פְּנֵ֣י הָֽאֲדָמָ֑ה וּבָנ֖וֹת יֻלְּד֥וּ לָהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was when began humankind to multiply on [the] face of the ground, and daughters were born to them,

en.L: And it happened, when {{gender:humankind|man}} began to multiply on the face of the ground and daughters were born to them,
en.B: When {{gender:people|men}} began to increase in number on the earth and daughters were born to them,
en.R: There came a time when there were many more people on the earth, and many daughters were born to them.

es.L: Y sucedió que, cuando {{gender:la humanidad|el hombre}} comenzó a multiplicarse sobre la superficie del suelo y les nacieron hijas,
es.B: Cuando {{gender:los seres humanos|los hombres}} comenzaron a multiplicarse sobre la tierra y les nacieron hijas,
es.R: Llegó un tiempo en que había mucha más gente en la tierra, y les nacieron muchas hijas.

decisions.choice: humankind: people in general
decisions.reason: The word is the one for humankind in 1:26 and 5:1-2, here people in general as they spread over the earth, fulfilling the command of 1:28.

decisions.choice: humankind (L), people (B); with the traditional setting, man or men
decisions.reason: As in 1:26, the word means human beings of both sexes, so the default is inclusive.

source.text: וַיִּרְא֤וּ בְנֵי־הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת־בְּנ֣וֹת הָֽאָדָ֔ם כִּ֥י טֹבֹ֖ת הֵ֑נָּה וַיִּקְח֤וּ לָהֶם֙ נָשִׁ֔ים מִכֹּ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּחָֽרוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw [the] sons of God the daughters of humankind, that good they [were], and they took for themselves wives from all whom they chose.

en.L: that the sons of God saw that the daughters of {{gender:humankind|man}} [were] beautiful, and they took for themselves wives from all whom they chose.
en.B: the sons of God saw that the daughters of {{gender:humans|men}} were beautiful, and they married any of them they chose.
en.R: The sons of God saw that these daughters were beautiful, and they took as wives any of them they wanted.

es.L: los hijos de Dios vieron que las hijas {{gender:de la humanidad|del hombre}} [eran] hermosas, y tomaron para sí mujeres de entre todas las que escogieron.
es.B: los hijos de Dios vieron que las hijas de {{gender:los seres humanos|los hombres}} eran hermosas, y tomaron como esposas a cuantas eligieron.
es.R: Los hijos de Dios vieron que esas hijas eran hermosas, y se casaron con las que quisieron.

decisions.choice: the sons of God: heavenly beings, most likely
alternatives: men of the godly line of Seth
decisions.reason: Elsewhere in the Old Testament "sons of God" names heavenly beings who serve God (Job 1:6; 2:1; 38:7; compare Psalm 29:1). Ancient Jewish writings and early Christian writers read the verse this way, and 1 Peter 3:19-20 and Jude 6 may allude to it. Others take the sons of God as the men of Seth's line marrying into Cain's, or as kings who claimed divine descent and took any women they wished. The text does not explain further.

decisions.choice: saw that they were good ... took: the pattern of 3:6
decisions.reason: The words echo 3:6, where the woman saw that the tree was good and took. Here too, seeing, desiring and taking cross a line God has set.

decisions.choice: beautiful
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is "good", which here means good-looking; the echo of 3:6 (m2) is noted in the decision.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֗ה לֹֽא־יָד֨וֹן רוּחִ֤י בָֽאָדָם֙ לְעֹלָ֔ם בְּשַׁגַּ֖ם ה֣וּא בָשָׂ֑ר וְהָי֣וּ יָמָ֔יו מֵאָ֥ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֖ים שָׁנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said YHWH, not will remain my spirit in humankind forever, since also he [is] flesh; and will be his days a hundred and twenty years.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said, "My spirit will not remain in {{gender:humankind|man}} forever, for {{gender:they are|he is}} indeed flesh; and {{gender:their|his}} days will be 120 years."
en.B: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said, "My spirit will not stay in {{gender:human beings|man}} forever, for they are mortal. Their days will be 120 years."
en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said, "I will not let {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} breath of life stay in people forever. They are only human. They will live no more than 120 years."

es.L: Y dijo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: «No permanecerá {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} espíritu en {{gender:los seres humanos|el hombre}} para siempre, porque ciertamente {{gender:ellos son|él es}} carne; y sus días serán 120 años».
es.B: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo: «Mi espíritu no permanecerá para siempre en {{gender:los seres humanos|el hombre}}, porque {{gender:son mortales|es mortal}}. Sus días serán 120 años».
es.R: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo: «No dejaré que {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} aliento de vida se quede para siempre en la gente. No son más que seres humanos. No vivirán más de 120 años».

decisions.choice: remain: stay, abide
decisions.reason: The verb occurs only here, and its meaning is uncertain. The ancient translations read "remain" or "abide", which fits the setting: the life-giving spirit God breathed into humankind (2:7) will not stay in them for ever. Others link it to a verb meaning "judge" or "contend".

decisions.choice: my spirit: the breath of life God gives
alternatives: the Holy Spirit striving with sinners
decisions.reason: The word means breath, wind or spirit. Here it is most likely the breath of life that God gives and can take away (2:7; 6:17; Psalm 104:29-30).

decisions.choice: his days will be 120 years: a limit on human life, or the time left before the flood
alternatives: a limit on the length of a human life
decisions.reason: The words can set the length of a human life (and lifespans do fall after the flood, toward this limit and below it: 11:10-32; Deuteronomy 34:7), or the time God allows before the flood. Both readings are old.

decisions.choice: they are mortal (B); They are only human (R)
decisions.reason: "Flesh" here means mortal, weak human nature (Psalm 78:39; Isaiah 40:6). Literal keeps "flesh".

decisions.choice: my (deity pronoun setting at Readable); My at the start of a sentence
decisions.reason: God speaks of himself, so "my" takes the deity pronoun setting; at the start of a sentence (Literal, Balanced) it is capitalised either way.

decisions.choice: "el SEÑOR" (default); with the divine name setting, "Yahvé"
decisions.reason: As in English, the name YHWH is "el SEÑOR" in small capitals by default, after the long tradition of reading "Lord" for the name; the setting gives the name itself in its usual modern Spanish form, "Yahvé". "Jehová" is a later hybrid form; plain "el Señor" would hide that a name stands here. The span takes in the article and any contraction ("del SEÑOR" / "de Yahvé", "al SEÑOR" / "a Yahvé"). This holds through the chapter.

decisions.choice: mi (deity pronoun setting)
decisions.reason: Spanish word order puts God's "my" inside the sentence at Literal ("No permanecerá mi espíritu") and Readable, so it takes the deity pronoun setting there; at Balanced it opens the sentence and is capitalised either way.

source.text: הַנְּפִלִ֞ים הָי֣וּ בָאָרֶץ֮ בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵם֒ וְגַ֣ם אַֽחֲרֵי־כֵ֗ן אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָבֹ֜אוּ בְּנֵ֤י הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ אֶל־בְּנ֣וֹת הָֽאָדָ֔ם וְיָלְד֖וּ לָהֶ֑ם הֵ֧מָּה הַגִּבֹּרִ֛ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר מֵעוֹלָ֖ם אַנְשֵׁ֥י הַשֵּֽׁם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: The Nephilim were on the earth in those days, and also afterward, when went in [the] sons of God to [the] daughters of humankind and they bore to them; they [were] the mighty men who [were] from of old, [the] men of the name.

en.L: The Nephilim were on the earth in those days, and also afterward, when the sons of God went in to the daughters of {{gender:humankind|man}} and they bore [children] to them. They [were] the mighty men who [were] of old, the men of renown.
en.B: The Nephilim were on the earth in those days, and also afterward, when the sons of God had relations with the daughters of {{gender:humans|men}} and they bore them children. These were the mighty men of old, the famous men.
en.R: In those days, and later too, there were giants on the earth called Nephilim. At that time the sons of God had children with the daughters of people. Those children grew up to be the famous heroes of long ago.

es.L: Los nefilim estaban en la tierra en aquellos días, y también después, cuando los hijos de Dios se unieron a las hijas {{gender:de la humanidad|del hombre}} y ellas les dieron [hijos]. Ellos [fueron] los valientes que [hubo] en la antigüedad, los hombres de renombre.
es.B: En aquellos días había nefilim en la tierra, y también después, cuando los hijos de Dios tuvieron relaciones con las hijas de {{gender:los seres humanos|los hombres}} y ellas les dieron hijos. Estos fueron los héroes de la antigüedad, hombres famosos.
es.R: En aquellos tiempos, y también más tarde, había en la tierra unos gigantes llamados nefilim. En esa época los hijos de Dios tuvieron hijos con las hijas de la gente. Esos hijos llegaron a ser los héroes famosos de tiempos antiguos.

decisions.choice: Nephilim: a people of great size and strength, left untranslated
decisions.reason: The word may come from the verb "to fall", but its meaning is not certain. Numbers 13:33 uses it for people of great size in Canaan, and the Septuagint translates it "giants". The verse does not say that the Nephilim were the children of the sons of God; it says they were on the earth at that time.

decisions.choice: the mighty men of old, the men of renown: famous warriors of the ancient past
decisions.reason: "Mighty men" are warriors and heroes (10:8-9). "Men of the name" means men with a great reputation. The next verses show what the world of such heroes had become.

decisions.choice: and also afterward: Nephilim were known after the flood too
decisions.reason: The words prepare for Numbers 13:33, where the Nephilim appear again in Canaan.

decisions.choice: giants ... called Nephilim
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name, following the Septuagint and Numbers 13:33 (m1).

decisions.choice: los nefilim (lower case)
decisions.reason: The word is left untranslated, as in English (m1), in its usual Spanish transcription. Spanish writes the names of peoples and kinds of beings in lower case ("los cananeos", "los querubines"), so "nefilim" is not capitalised. Readable explains it, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: se unieron a
decisions.reason: The Hebrew idiom "go in to" a woman means to have sexual relations. A word-for-word "entraron a" does not carry that sense in Spanish, and "se llegaron a" is archaic, so Literal uses "se unieron a"; Balanced says it plainly, as the English Balanced does.

source.text: וַיַּ֣רְא יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֥י רַבָּ֛ה רָעַ֥ת הָאָדָ֖ם בָּאָ֑רֶץ וְכָל־יֵ֨צֶר֙ מַחְשְׁבֹ֣ת לִבּ֔וֹ רַ֥ק רַ֖ע כָּל־הַיּֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw YHWH that great [was] the evil of humankind on the earth, and every inclination of [the] thoughts of his heart [was] only evil all the day.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} saw that the wickedness of {{gender:humankind|man}} [was] great on the earth, and every inclination of the thoughts of his heart [was] only evil all the day.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} saw how great the wickedness of {{gender:the human race|man}} had become on the earth, and that every inclination of the thoughts of their hearts was only evil all the time.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} saw how evil people on earth had become. Everything they thought about and planned was evil all the time.

es.L: Y vio {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} que la maldad {{gender:de la humanidad|del hombre}} [era] grande en la tierra, y que toda inclinación de los pensamientos de su corazón [era] solo mal todo el día.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} vio cuán grande se había vuelto la maldad {{gender:del género humano|del hombre}} en la tierra, y que toda intención de los pensamientos de su corazón era siempre solamente mala.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} vio lo malvada que se había vuelto la gente en la tierra. Todo lo que pensaban y planeaban era malo todo el tiempo.

decisions.choice: every inclination of the thoughts of his heart: all that people planned and intended
decisions.reason: "Inclination" is from the verb "form" of 2:7: what the mind shapes or plans. The heart in Hebrew is the center of thought and will, not only of feeling. The verse piles up words, every, only, all the day, to say that evil had filled everything. 8:21 says the same after the flood.

decisions.choice: the LORD saw that great was the evil: the reverse of 1:31
decisions.reason: In 1:31 God saw everything he had made, and it was very good. Now he sees that human evil is great.

decisions.choice: inclinación (L); intención (B)
decisions.reason: The word is what the mind forms or plans (m1). Literal keeps "inclinación" beside the English "inclination"; Balanced says "intención", the plainer word for what someone means to do.

source.text: וַיִּנָּ֣חֶם יְהוָ֔ה כִּֽי־עָשָׂ֥ה אֶת־הָֽאָדָ֖ם בָּאָ֑רֶץ וַיִּתְעַצֵּ֖ב אֶל־לִבּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And regretted YHWH that he had made humankind on the earth, and he was grieved to his heart.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} regretted that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had made {{gender:humankind|man}} on the earth, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was grieved to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} heart.
en.B: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} regretted that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had made {{gender:human beings|man}} on the earth, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} heart was deeply troubled.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was sorry that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had made people on the earth. It hurt {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} heart deeply.

es.L: Y lamentó {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} haber hecho {{gender:a la humanidad|al hombre}} en la tierra, y sintió dolor en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} corazón.
es.B: Entonces {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} le pesó haber hecho {{gender:a los seres humanos|al hombre}} en la tierra, y {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} corazón se llenó de dolor.
es.R: {{divine_name:Al SEÑOR|A Yahvé}} le dio mucha tristeza haber hecho a la gente en la tierra. Eso {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dolió profundamente en el corazón.

decisions.choice: regretted: God's sorrow, said in human terms
decisions.reason: The verb, the one Lamech used in naming Noah (5:29), means to be sorry, to grieve or to change one's course. The Bible says God does not change his mind as a human does (Numbers 23:19; 1 Samuel 15:29), yet it often speaks of him relenting or regretting (Exodus 32:14; Jonah 3:10). Here it shows that human evil truly grieves God; it does not mean he made a mistake or did not foresee it.

decisions.choice: grieved to his heart: deeply pained
decisions.reason: The verb is related to the "pain" of 3:16-17: the pain of the woman and the toil of the man. Now God himself feels pain at what humankind has done.

decisions.choice: lamentó (L); le pesó (B); le dio mucha tristeza (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is God's sorrow and grief, said in human terms (m1). In current Spanish "arrepentirse" mostly means repenting of a wrong one has done, which is not the point here, so the levels use words of regret and sorrow. The same choice is made for "I regret" in verse 7.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֗ה אֶמְחֶ֨ה אֶת־הָאָדָ֤ם אֲשֶׁר־בָּרָ֨אתִי֙ מֵעַל֙ פְּנֵ֣י הָֽאֲדָמָ֔ה מֵֽאָדָם֙ עַד־בְּהֵמָ֔ה עַד־רֶ֖מֶשׂ וְעַד־ע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם כִּ֥י נִחַ֖מְתִּי כִּ֥י עֲשִׂיתִֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said YHWH, I will wipe out humankind whom I created from on [the] face of the ground, from humankind to animal[s], to creeping thing[s], and to [the] bird[s] of the heavens, for I regret that I made them.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said, "I will wipe out {{gender:humankind|man}} whom I created from the face of the ground, from {{gender:humankind|man}} to animals, to creeping things, and to the birds of the heavens, for I regret that I made them."
en.B: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said, "I will wipe from the face of the earth the human beings I have created, and with them the animals, the creatures that move along the ground and the birds of the sky, for I regret that I made them."
en.R: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said, "I will wipe out the people I created. I will remove them from the earth, along with the animals, the creatures that crawl and the birds of the sky. I am sorry I made them."

es.L: Y dijo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: «Borraré {{gender:a la humanidad|al hombre}} que creé de la superficie del suelo, desde {{gender:la humanidad|el hombre}} hasta los animales, hasta los seres que se arrastran y hasta las aves de los cielos, porque lamento haberlos hecho».
es.B: Por eso {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo: «Borraré de la faz de la tierra a los seres humanos que he creado, y con ellos a los animales, a los seres que se arrastran por el suelo y a las aves del cielo, porque me pesa haberlos hecho».
es.R: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo: «Voy a borrar a la gente que creé. La quitaré de la tierra, junto con los animales, las criaturas que se arrastran y las aves del cielo. Siento mucho haberlos hecho».

decisions.choice: wipe out: wipe away, blot out
decisions.reason: The verb means to wipe clean, as a dish is wiped (2 Kings 21:13), or to blot out a name from a record (Exodus 32:32). The flood will wash the earth clean.

decisions.choice: from humankind to animals: the animals share the judgment
decisions.reason: The animals were given to humankind's rule (1:26-28), so they share its fate. The list runs through the creatures of the sixth and fifth days in reverse, as if creation were being undone.

source.text: וְנֹ֕חַ מָ֥צָא חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: But Noah found favor in [the] eyes of YHWH.

en.L: But Noah found favor in the eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: But Noah found favor with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was pleased with Noah.

es.L: Pero Noé halló favor a los ojos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.B: Pero Noé contó con el favor {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.R: Pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} estaba contento con Noé.

decisions.choice: found favor: received grace and kindness
decisions.reason: The word means favor or grace, kindness that is given, not earned. In Hebrew its two consonants are those of Noah's name reversed, a small play on words.

decisions.choice: favor
decisions.reason: "Favor" is the usual English for this phrase ("find favor in the eyes of"). The word is the Old Testament's word for grace; "grace" as a key term belongs to the Greek word.

source.text: אֵ֚לֶּה תּוֹלְדֹ֣ת נֹ֔חַ נֹ֗חַ אִ֥ישׁ צַדִּ֛יק תָּמִ֥ים הָיָ֖ה בְּדֹֽרֹתָ֑יו אֶת־הָֽאֱלֹהִ֖ים הִֽתְהַלֶּךְ־נֹֽחַ׃

records.literal_gloss: These [are the] generations of Noah. Noah [was] a man righteous, blameless he was among his generations; with God walked Noah.

en.L: These [are] the generations of Noah. Noah was a righteous man, blameless in his generations; Noah walked with God.
en.B: This is the story of Noah. Noah was a righteous man, blameless among the people of his time, and he walked with God.
en.R: This is the story of Noah. Noah did what was right and lived a good life, unlike the other people of his time. He was close to God.

es.L: Estas [son] las generaciones de Noé. Noé era un hombre justo, intachable entre sus generaciones; Noé caminaba con Dios.
es.B: Esta es la historia de Noé. Noé era un hombre justo, intachable entre la gente de su tiempo, y caminaba con Dios.
es.R: Esta es la historia de Noé. Noé hacía lo correcto y vivía una vida buena, a diferencia de las demás personas de su tiempo. Vivía muy unido a Dios.

decisions.choice: righteous: doing what is right in God's eyes
decisions.reason: Noah is the first person in the Bible called righteous: one who does what is right and faithful toward God and others. Ezekiel 14:14 names him with Daniel and Job, and Hebrews 11:7 says he became "an heir of the righteousness that comes by faith".

decisions.choice: blameless: whole, of complete integrity
decisions.reason: The word means whole or complete; it is used of sacrificial animals without defect (Exodus 12:5). Of a person it means integrity, not sinlessness (9:21 shows Noah's failing).

decisions.choice: walked with God: as Enoch did
decisions.reason: The words are those used of Enoch (5:22, 24). Noah lives in close fellowship with God in an age of corruption.

decisions.choice: did what was right and lived a good life
decisions.reason: Readable says what "righteous" and "blameless" mean (m1, m2).

source.text: וַיּ֥וֹלֶד נֹ֖חַ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה בָנִ֑ים אֶת־שֵׁ֖ם אֶת־חָ֥ם וְאֶת־יָֽפֶת׃

records.literal_gloss: And fathered Noah three sons, Shem, Ham and Japheth.

en.L: And Noah fathered three sons: Shem, Ham and Japheth.
en.B: Noah had three sons: Shem, Ham and Japheth.
en.R: Noah had three sons, named Shem, Ham and Japheth.

es.L: Y engendró Noé tres hijos: Sem, Cam y Jafet.
es.B: Noé tuvo tres hijos: Sem, Cam y Jafet.
es.R: Noé tuvo tres hijos, que se llamaban Sem, Cam y Jafet.

source.text: וַתִּשָּׁחֵ֥ת הָאָ֖רֶץ לִפְנֵ֣י הָֽאֱלֹהִ֑ים וַתִּמָּלֵ֥א הָאָ֖רֶץ חָמָֽס׃

records.literal_gloss: And was corrupt the earth before God, and was filled the earth [with] violence.

en.L: And the earth was corrupt before God, and the earth was filled [with] violence.
en.B: Now the earth was corrupt in God's sight and full of violence.
en.R: God saw that the world was rotten. It was full of violence.

es.L: Y la tierra se corrompió delante de Dios, y la tierra se llenó [de] violencia.
es.B: La tierra estaba corrompida ante Dios y llena de violencia.
es.R: Dios vio que el mundo se había echado a perder. Estaba lleno de violencia.

decisions.choice: corrupt: ruined, spoiled
decisions.reason: The verb means to ruin or spoil, as a pot is spoiled (Jeremiah 13:7; 18:4). It is used four times in verses 11-13 and once more in verse 17: the earth has ruined itself, and God will ruin (destroy) it.

decisions.choice: violence: wrongdoing that harms others
decisions.reason: The word (chamas) means violence and injustice, the strong harming the weak. It is the sin named in the account of the flood, and the opposite of the rule given in 1:26-28.

decisions.choice: se había echado a perder
decisions.reason: The verb means to ruin or spoil (m1). "Echarse a perder" is the everyday Spanish for something spoiled, and it is what Readable uses where the English Readable says "rotten".

source.text: וַיַּ֧רְא אֱלֹהִ֛ים אֶת־הָאָ֖רֶץ וְהִנֵּ֣ה נִשְׁחָ֑תָה כִּֽי־הִשְׁחִ֧ית כָּל־בָּשָׂ֛ר אֶת־דַּרְכּ֖וֹ עַל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And saw God the earth, and behold, it was corrupt, for had corrupted all flesh its way on the earth.

en.L: And God saw the earth, and look, it was corrupt, for all flesh had corrupted its way on the earth.
en.B: God saw how corrupt the earth had become, for all the people on earth had corrupted their ways.
en.R: God looked at the world and saw how rotten it was. All the people on earth had turned to evil ways.

es.L: Y vio Dios la tierra, y, mira, se había corrompido, porque toda carne había corrompido su camino en la tierra.
es.B: Dios vio cuán corrompida estaba la tierra, porque toda la gente de la tierra había corrompido su manera de vivir.
es.R: Dios miró el mundo y vio cuánto se había echado a perder. Toda la gente de la tierra se había ido por malos caminos.

decisions.choice: all flesh: all living creatures, or all people
decisions.reason: "All flesh" can mean every living creature (6:17, 19) or all humankind (Isaiah 40:5). Here "corrupted its way" points chiefly to human beings, whose violence spoils the whole earth.

decisions.choice: God saw ... and look: the words of 1:31
decisions.reason: In 1:31 God saw all he had made, "and look, it was very good". Now he looks, and it is corrupt.

decisions.choice: all the people on earth
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "people", the main sense here (m1); Literal keeps "all flesh".

decisions.choice: mira
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew "look" (m2) with "mira", as the English Literal says "look"; "he aquí" is archaic. The same holds in verses 13 and 17.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֜ים לְנֹ֗חַ קֵ֤ץ כָּל־בָּשָׂר֙ בָּ֣א לְפָנַ֔י כִּֽי־מָלְאָ֥ה הָאָ֛רֶץ חָמָ֖ס מִפְּנֵיהֶ֑ם וְהִנְנִ֥י מַשְׁחִיתָ֖ם אֶת־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said God to Noah, [the] end of all flesh has come before me, for filled is the earth [with] violence because of them; and here I [am] destroying them with the earth.

en.L: And God said to Noah, "The end of all flesh has come before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, for the earth is filled [with] violence because of them; and look, I am about to destroy them with the earth.
en.B: So God said to Noah, "I have decided to put an end to all people, for the earth is filled with violence because of them. I am going to destroy them along with the earth.
en.R: So God said to Noah, "I am going to put an end to all people. The earth is full of their violence. So I am going to destroy them, and the earth with them.

es.L: Y dijo Dios a Noé: «El fin de toda carne ha llegado delante de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, porque la tierra está llena [de] violencia por causa de ellos; y, mira, voy a destruirlos junto con la tierra.
es.B: Entonces Dios dijo a Noé: «He decidido acabar con toda la gente, porque por su culpa la tierra está llena de violencia. Voy a destruirlos junto con la tierra.
es.R: Entonces Dios le dijo a Noé: «Voy a acabar con toda la gente. La tierra está llena de su violencia. Por eso voy a destruirlos, y a la tierra con ellos.

decisions.choice: the end of all flesh has come before me: I have decided to bring it to an end
decisions.reason: To come before God is to come to his attention for a decision, like a case before a judge. The same language of "the end" is used by the prophets (Amos 8:2; Ezekiel 7:2-3).

decisions.choice: destroy them with the earth: the verb of verses 11-12
decisions.reason: "Destroy" is the same verb as "corrupt" in verses 11-12: they have ruined the earth, and God will ruin them with it. His judgment matches what they have done.

decisions.choice: I have decided to put an end to all people
alternatives: The end of all flesh has come before me
decisions.reason: Balanced says what the idiom means (m1); Literal keeps it, with "me" under the deity pronoun setting.

source.text: עֲשֵׂ֤ה לְךָ֙ תֵּבַ֣ת עֲצֵי־גֹ֔פֶר קִנִּ֖ים תַּֽעֲשֶׂ֣ה אֶת־הַתֵּבָ֑ה וְכָֽפַרְתָּ֥ אֹתָ֛הּ מִבַּ֥יִת וּמִח֖וּץ בַּכֹּֽפֶר׃

records.literal_gloss: Make for yourself an ark of gopher wood; rooms you will make the ark, and you will cover it from inside and from outside with pitch.

en.L: Make for yourself an ark of gopher wood; you will make the ark [with] rooms, and you will cover it inside and outside with pitch.
en.B: Make yourself an ark of gopher wood. Make rooms in it, and coat it inside and out with pitch.
en.R: Build a huge boat out of good wood. Make rooms in it, and cover it inside and outside with tar so that water cannot get in.

es.L: Hazte un arca de madera de gofer; harás el arca [con] compartimentos, y la cubrirás por dentro y por fuera con brea.
es.B: Hazte un arca de madera de gofer. Hazle compartimentos, y recúbrela de brea por dentro y por fuera.
es.R: Construye un arca, un barco enorme, con buena madera. Hazle cuartos por dentro, y cúbrela de brea por dentro y por fuera para que no le entre el agua.

decisions.choice: ark: a chest-shaped boat
decisions.reason: The word is used only for Noah's ark and for the basket in which the baby Moses was saved (Exodus 2:3, 5). Both are vessels in which God preserves life through the water. It is a box-like craft, built to float rather than to sail.

decisions.choice: gopher wood: a kind of wood not known today
decisions.reason: The word occurs only here. It may be cypress or another resinous wood; the ancient translations only guessed. It is left as "gopher wood".

decisions.choice: rooms: compartments
alternatives: reeds (a different reading of the consonants)
decisions.reason: The word means "nests", here the compartments inside the ark. Some read the same consonants as "reeds", used with pitch to seal it.

decisions.choice: cover with pitch: seal against the water
decisions.reason: The verb and the noun come from the same root (kafar, kofer): "cover it with covering". Pitch is a tar-like sealant. The same root later means "atone" (Leviticus 17:11), though that is not its sense here.

decisions.choice: good wood
decisions.reason: Readable does not use a name few readers would know (m2); "good wood" says only what the text implies.

decisions.choice: un arca, el arca (every level; Readable adds "un barco enorme" the first time)
decisions.reason: "Arca" is the traditional Spanish word for Noah's vessel and, like the Hebrew, also means a chest or box (m1). The English Readable says "boat"; Spanish Readable keeps "el arca", explained once as "un barco enorme", so that the familiar name stays in view through the flood story. Settled for Genesis 6-9.

decisions.choice: madera de gofer
decisions.reason: The kind of wood is unknown (m2), so the word is transcribed, as the English "gopher wood" does. Readable says "buena madera", as the English Readable says "good wood".

decisions.choice: compartimentos (L, B), cuartos (R); brea
decisions.reason: "Compartimentos" names the divisions inside the ark (m3); Readable says "cuartos", the plain word for rooms. "Brea" is the common Spanish for pitch or tar used to seal a boat (m4), plain enough for every level.

source.text: וְזֶ֕ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּֽעֲשֶׂ֖ה אֹתָ֑הּ שְׁלֹ֧שׁ מֵא֣וֹת אַמָּ֗ה אֹ֚רֶךְ הַתֵּבָ֔ה חֲמִשִּׁ֤ים אַמָּה֙ רָחְבָּ֔הּ וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים אַמָּ֖ה קוֹמָתָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And this [is] how you will make it: three hundred cubit[s] the length of the ark, fifty cubit[s] its width, and thirty cubit[s] its height.

en.L: And this [is] how you will make it: the length of the ark 300 cubits, its width fifty cubits, and its height thirty cubits.
en.B: This is how you are to make it: the ark is to be {{units:450 feet|300 cubits}} long, {{units:75 feet|fifty cubits}} wide and {{units:45 feet|thirty cubits}} high.
en.R: This is how big to make it: {{units:450 feet|300 cubits}} long, {{units:75 feet|fifty cubits}} wide and {{units:45 feet|thirty cubits}} high.

es.L: Y así [es como] la harás: la longitud del arca, 300 codos; su anchura, cincuenta codos; y su altura, treinta codos.
es.B: Así es como debes hacerla: el arca tendrá {{units:135 metros|300 codos}} de largo, {{units:22,5 metros|cincuenta codos}} de ancho y {{units:13,5 metros|treinta codos}} de alto.
es.R: Así de grande debes hacerla: {{units:135 metros|300 codos}} de largo, {{units:22,5 metros|cincuenta codos}} de ancho y {{units:13,5 metros|treinta codos}} de alto.

decisions.choice: cubit: about 18 inches (45 centimeters)
decisions.reason: A cubit was the length from the elbow to the fingertip, about 18 inches or 45 centimeters. The ark was about 450 by 75 by 45 feet (about 135 by 22 by 13 meters): very large, and in the proportions of a steady, box-like barge.

decisions.choice: 450 feet, 75 feet, 45 feet; with the Measures setting, cubits
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give modern measures by default and the original cubits as the setting's alternative; Literal keeps cubits.

decisions.choice: 135 metros, 22,5 metros, 13,5 metros; with the Measures setting, codos
decisions.reason: Spanish readers measure in metres, so Balanced and Readable give metric measures by default (at 45 centimetres to the cubit, m1) where the English gives feet; the setting gives the original cubits. Literal keeps the cubits. The same applies to the cubit in verse 16 ("medio metro").

source.text: צֹ֣הַר׀תַּֽעֲשֶׂ֣ה לַתֵּבָ֗ה וְאֶל־אַמָּה֙ תְּכַלֶ֣נָּהמִלְמַ֔עְלָה וּפֶ֥תַח הַתֵּבָ֖ה בְּצִדָּ֣הּ תָּשִׂ֑ים תַּחְתִּיִּ֛ם שְׁנִיִּ֥ם וּשְׁלִשִׁ֖ים תַּֽעֲשֶֽׂהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: A roof you will make for the ark, and to a cubit you will finish it from above; and [the] entrance of the ark in its side you will put; lower, second and third [decks] you will make it.

en.L: A roof you will make for the ark, and to a cubit you will finish it above; and the entrance of the ark you will put in its side; [with] lower, second and third [decks] you will make it.
en.B: Make a roof for the ark and finish it to {{units:18 inches|a cubit}} from the top. Put a door in the side of the ark, and make it with lower, middle and upper decks.
en.R: Make a roof for it, with an opening {{units:18 inches|a cubit}} high just below the roof all around. Put a door in the side. Build the boat with three decks: a bottom deck, a middle deck and an upper deck.

es.L: Un techo harás al arca, y a un codo la terminarás por arriba; y la entrada del arca pondrás en su costado; [con pisos] inferior, segundo y tercero la harás.
es.B: Hazle un techo al arca y termínala a {{units:medio metro|un codo}} de la parte de arriba. Pon una puerta en el costado del arca, y hazla con un piso inferior, uno intermedio y uno superior.
es.R: Hazle un techo, con una abertura de {{units:medio metro|un codo}} de alto justo debajo del techo, todo alrededor. Pon una puerta en un costado. Construye el arca con tres pisos: uno abajo, uno en medio y uno arriba.

decisions.choice: roof: a covering over the ark
decisions.reason: The word occurs only here. It may mean a roof, or an opening for light (it sounds like the word for "noon"). The instruction to finish it "to a cubit from above" may describe a gap of a cubit between roof and walls to let in light and air.

decisions.choice: lower, second and third: three decks
decisions.reason: The ark has three levels. The words "decks" or "stories" are understood.

decisions.choice: an opening a cubit high just below the roof all around
alternatives: finish it to a cubit from above
decisions.reason: Readable follows one likely reading of an obscure phrase (m1).

decisions.choice: techo
decisions.reason: The word occurs only here and may mean a roof or an opening for light (m1). Spanish follows the English "roof" with "techo"; Readable describes the opening below it, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: pisos
decisions.reason: The three levels of the ark are understood (m2). "Pisos" is the plain word for the storeys of a building; "cubiertas" is the term for a ship's decks, but it suits a sailing ship more than a box-like vessel, and young readers know it less.

source.text: וַאֲנִ֗י הִנְנִי֩ מֵבִ֨יא אֶת־הַמַּבּ֥וּל מַ֨יִם֙ עַל־הָאָ֔רֶץ לְשַׁחֵ֣ת כָּל־בָּשָׂ֗ר אֲשֶׁר־בּוֹ֙ ר֣וּחַ חַיִּ֔ים מִתַּ֖חַת הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם כֹּ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־בָּאָ֖רֶץ יִגְוָֽע׃

records.literal_gloss: And I, here I [am] bringing the flood, water on the earth, to destroy all flesh in which [is the] breath of life from under the heavens; all that [is] on the earth will perish.

en.L: And I, look, I am bringing the flood, water on the earth, to destroy all flesh in which [is] the breath of life from under the heavens; all that [is] on the earth will perish.
en.B: For {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} part, I am about to bring the flood, water over the earth, to destroy from under the sky every creature that has the breath of life in it. Everything on earth will die.
en.R: I am going to send a flood of water over the earth. It will destroy every living creature under the sky that breathes. Everything on earth will die.

es.L: Y yo, mira, yo voy a traer el diluvio, agua sobre la tierra, para destruir toda carne en la que [hay] aliento de vida debajo de los cielos; todo lo que [hay] en la tierra perecerá.
es.B: Por {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} parte, voy a traer el diluvio, agua sobre la tierra, para destruir bajo el cielo a toda criatura que tiene aliento de vida. Todo cuanto hay en la tierra morirá.
es.R: Voy a enviar un diluvio, una gran inundación que cubrirá la tierra. Destruirá a todos los seres vivos que respiran bajo el cielo. Todo lo que vive en la tierra morirá.

decisions.choice: the flood: a word used only for this flood
decisions.reason: The word (mabbul) is used in the Bible only for Noah's flood (and in Psalm 29:10, which recalls it). "Water" is added to say what the flood is. The waters of chapter 1 that God held back now return.

decisions.choice: and I, look, I: God's emphasis on his own action
decisions.reason: "I" is said twice: God himself brings the flood. The flood is his act of judgment, not a natural accident.

decisions.choice: the breath of life: the gift of 2:7
decisions.reason: The phrase recalls the breath of life God breathed into the man (2:7) and the spirit of 6:3: what God gave, he takes back.

decisions.choice: el diluvio (every level; Readable adds "una gran inundación")
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is used only for this flood (m1), and Spanish has a word kept for it too: "el diluvio". Readable explains it once as a great flood of water, as the English Readable says "a flood of water". Settled for Genesis 6-11.

source.text: וַהֲקִמֹתִ֥י אֶת־בְּרִיתִ֖י אִתָּ֑ךְ וּבָאתָ֙ אֶל־הַתֵּבָ֔ה אַתָּ֕ה וּבָנֶ֛יךָ וְאִשְׁתְּךָ֥ וּנְשֵֽׁי־בָנֶ֖יךָ אִתָּֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will establish my covenant with you, and you will come into the ark, you and your sons and your wife and the wives of your sons with you.

en.L: But I will establish {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant with you, and you will come into the ark, you and your sons and your wife and your sons' wives with you.
en.B: But I will establish {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant with you, and you will enter the ark: you, your sons, your wife and your sons' wives with you.
en.R: But I will make a covenant with you. You will go into the boat with your wife, your sons and their wives.

es.L: Pero estableceré {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pacto contigo, y entrarás al arca, tú y tus hijos y tu esposa y las esposas de tus hijos contigo.
es.B: Pero contigo estableceré {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pacto: entrarás al arca tú con tus hijos, tu esposa y las esposas de tus hijos.
es.R: Pero yo haré un pacto contigo. Entrarás en el arca con tu esposa, tus hijos y las esposas de ellos.

decisions.choice: I will establish my covenant with you: the first time the word covenant appears
alternatives: I will keep the covenant I already made
decisions.reason: A covenant is a binding commitment between two parties, here God's solemn promise. This is the first time the word appears in the Bible. The covenant itself is set out after the flood (9:8-17). The verb "establish" can mean to set up a new covenant or to confirm one.

decisions.choice: make a covenant
decisions.reason: Readable says "make", which young readers will follow more easily than "establish".

decisions.choice: pacto
decisions.reason: This is the first time "covenant" appears (m1). "Pacto" is the plain Spanish word for a binding agreement and is understood by young readers; "alianza", also used in Spanish Bibles, leans toward a political alliance in everyday speech. Settled for Genesis.

source.text: וּמִכָּל־הָ֠חַי מִֽכָּל־בָּשָׂ֞ר שְׁנַ֧יִם מִכֹּ֛ל תָּבִ֥יא אֶל־הַתֵּבָ֖ה לְהַחֲיֹ֣ת אִתָּ֑ךְ זָכָ֥ר וּנְקֵבָ֖ה יִֽהְיֽוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And of every living thing, of all flesh, two of each you will bring into the ark to keep alive with you; male and female they will be.

en.L: And of every living thing, of all flesh, you will bring two of every kind into the ark to keep [them] alive with you; they will be male and female.
en.B: Bring into the ark two of every living creature, a male and a female, to keep them alive with you.
en.R: Bring two of every kind of animal into the boat, a male and a female, so that they will stay alive with you.

es.L: Y de todo ser viviente, de toda carne, meterás en el arca dos de cada [clase] para conservar[los] con vida contigo; macho y hembra serán.
es.B: Mete en el arca a dos de cada ser viviente, un macho y una hembra, para que conserven la vida contigo.
es.R: Mete en el arca dos animales de cada clase, un macho y una hembra, para que sigan vivos contigo.

decisions.choice: two of every kind, male and female: enough to begin again
decisions.reason: A male and a female of every kind are kept alive to fill the earth again. In 7:2-3 God gives a fuller instruction: seven pairs of clean animals and birds, needed also for sacrifice after the flood (8:20).

source.text: מֵהָע֣וֹף לְמִינֵ֗הוּ וּמִן־הַבְּהֵמָה֙ לְמִינָ֔הּ מִכֹּ֛ל רֶ֥מֶשׂ הָֽאֲדָמָ֖ה לְמִינֵ֑הוּ שְׁנַ֧יִם מִכֹּ֛ל יָבֹ֥אוּ אֵלֶ֖יךָ לְהַֽחֲיֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: Of the bird[s] according to its kind, and of the animal[s] according to its kind, of every creeping thing of the ground according to its kind, two of each will come to you, to keep alive.

en.L: Of the birds according to their kind, and of the animals according to their kind, of every creeping thing of the ground according to its kind, two of every kind will come to you to keep [them] alive.
en.B: Two of every kind of bird, of every kind of animal and of every kind of creature that moves along the ground will come to you, to be kept alive.
en.R: Two of every kind of bird, every kind of animal and every kind of small creature will come to you, so that you can keep them alive.

es.L: De las aves según su especie, y de los animales según su especie, de todo lo que se arrastra por el suelo según su especie, dos de cada [clase] vendrán a ti para conservar[los] con vida.
es.B: Vendrán a ti dos de cada especie de ave, de cada especie de animal y de cada especie de criatura que se arrastra por el suelo, para que se conserven con vida.
es.R: Vendrán a ti dos de cada clase de ave, de cada clase de animal y de cada clase de animalito, para que los mantengas con vida.

decisions.choice: according to its kind: the words of chapter 1
decisions.reason: The phrase of 1:11-25 returns: the kinds God created will be kept.

decisions.choice: will come to you: the animals come of themselves
decisions.reason: Noah does not have to hunt for them: they will come to him (7:9, 15).

source.text: וְאַתָּ֣ה קַח־לְךָ֗ מִכָּל־מַֽאֲכָל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֵֽאָכֵ֔ל וְאָסַפְתָּ֖ אֵלֶ֑יךָ וְהָיָ֥ה לְךָ֛ וְלָהֶ֖ם לְאָכְלָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And you, take for yourself of all food which is eaten, and gather [it] to yourself, and it will be for you and for them for food.

en.L: And you, take for yourself of all food that is eaten, and gather [it] to yourself, and it will be food for you and for them."
en.B: Take with you every kind of food that is eaten and store it up, to be food for you and for them."
en.R: Take every kind of food that you and the animals eat, and store it on the boat for all of you."

es.L: Y tú, toma para ti de todo alimento que se come, y [lo] almacenarás contigo, y será alimento para ti y para ellos».
es.B: Lleva contigo toda clase de alimentos que se comen, y almacénalos, para que sirvan de alimento para ti y para ellos».
es.R: Lleva toda clase de comida de la que comen tú y los animales, y guárdala en el arca para que todos tengan qué comer».

source.text: וַיַּ֖עַשׂ נֹ֑חַ כְּ֠כֹל אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֥ה אֹת֛וֹ אֱלֹהִ֖ים כֵּ֥ן עָשָֽׂה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And did Noah according to all that commanded him God; so he did.

en.L: And Noah did according to all that God commanded him; so he did.
en.B: Noah did everything just as God commanded him.
en.R: Noah did everything God told him to do.

es.L: E hizo Noé conforme a todo lo que Dios le mandó; así hizo.
es.B: Noé hizo todo tal como Dios le había mandado.
es.R: Noé hizo todo lo que Dios le dijo.

decisions.choice: Noah did all that God commanded him: complete obedience
decisions.reason: The statement is repeated (7:5, 9, 16) and echoes the building of the tabernacle (Exodus 39:32, 42-43; 40:16). Noah's righteousness (verse 9) shows itself in obedience. Hebrews 11:7 calls this obedience an act of faith.
